text.p: Britain's United Utilities plc indicated on Thursday that it felt a level of leakage at 15 percent of supplies would be an economical level, compared with current levels of 24 percent for the company.
"Below 15 percent would be very difficult and very expensive to achieve," chairman Sir Desmond Pitcher told a press conference.
The company has cut leakage to current levels of 24 percent from 30 percent in 1994/95.
An "economic" level is that considered to be economically achievable and acceptable to customers.

Water companies have been told by the new Labour government that they will face mandatory leakage targets as part of a 10-point plan aimed at improvements to deal with the country's worst drought in 200 years.
United's chief executive Brian Staples earlier told Reuters in an interview that the company was "highly compliant with the 10 points."
He added that industry regulator Ofwat had singled United out "as having made excellent progress in controlling leakage."
Companies have been asked to respond to the government's plan within three weeks of a crisis summit which was held on May 19.

Pitcher reiterated the company's hope that actions it had taken to share benefits among shareholders and customers would be taken into account when the government decides how to impose a planned one-off tax on the "excess profits" of privatised utilities.
"I sincerely hope (the government) recognise that (sharing) and do not remove the opportunity" to share between customer and shareholder, he said.
Pitcher added he would like to see the proposed tax "spread as far as possible across those companies that have regulated activities," but declined to give specific names.
The new Labour government's plans for the tax were a central plank of the manifesto which brought it a landslide victory on May 1, but details await a first budget, possibly in July.
Executives added United aimed to launch an energy company to tackle liberalisation of gas and electricity markets scheduled for 1998 soon but declined to give further details.
